What you're doing, using a keyword list, is impossible for finding directories.

The server in question had responded to me with a TTL of 64, so likely Linux and definitely not Windows. This means directory names are case sensitive. Assuming a maximum directory length of 10 characters of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, thats 10^62 possible directories (you scanned about 1/3x10^14 of the possible directories)

You literally cannot find the directories without A) hacking the server or B) testing each possible directory name. In the case of your tests, every result was an HTTP 400 - which was also the results I got testing any directory (including /BIGFATEPICMEME and the root directory).

Your test results are worthless unless you want to know that the directory /yahoo/ is just the same as every other result.

21 year old female, 5'6" and 118 lbs. I would like to put on a little bit of weight, about 10 lbs or so, as none of my designer jeans fit anymore, everything is so baggy. How do I gain weight/muscle w/o gaining flab and celulite? Gym membership is not an option at the moment and I have a $600 monthly food budget for my family of 4 (two children and a fiance) Please help !
Would like to gain some weight w/o turning into a flabflapper

I'm not a trainer, just good at watching myself. Eat good protein and up your calories by a margin that is a little greater than your tdee. Same stuff as you currently eat, if it is balanced, combined with a good body weight program if you can't make it to the gym, and you'll be fine. Just gain it slowly so that you don't go overboard and mess up your skin or hair. Good luck!

1. Calculate your TDEE

  2. Eat at a caloric surplus of 100-200 calories per day. Start at 100 (so if your TDEE is 1600 calories, eat 1700 per day). Once your progress stagnates for a couple of weeks increase by 200 calories. Every time you gain 5 pounds that is consistent between weighings/at different times of day, recalculate your TDEE. Your weight will fluctuate a few pounds naturally, so be sure to measure it often.

  3. At the same time, start a lifting program. Gaining 10 pounds of just fat will likely lead to skinny-fat syndrome. Since you said a gym membership isn't possible right now you will of course need to work out at home. There's nothing preventing you from building a great body without a gym. But since budget is an issue I'd recommend something like this:

Workouts=> Monday, Wednesday, Friday

Routine=> Pull-up/Chin-up: 3 sets x 8-12 reps *You will need a door mounted pullup bar to do these on; you can get one at WalMart for around 20$. If money is really tight, use the monkey bars at a local park.

Squats: 3 sets x 8-12 reps

Pushups: 3 sets 8-12 reps

Abs: 3 sets of crunches x 10-15 reps

-If you've never trained before, you might not be able to do any pullups/chinups. So you will do reverse sets instead, you will use something to get you to the top position of rep, then slowly lower yourself down. This video explains how to do this: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mRznU6pzez0/watch?v=3ktRmhr2IWE

-Once you can do 15 of each with good form, you will need to add weight. Hopefully by then you will have either met your goal, or will have enough disposable income for a gym membership or some home-gym equipment.

  1. Nutrition: Apart from that small caloric surplus you will need adequate protein. I recommend at least 0.8 grams of protein per pound of body weight per day. More than that is fine, but don't eat less. Starting at 118 pounds you will want 95 grams of protein per day.

  2. You will have to keep working out once you've met your goal to keep any muscle you've gained, but you won't need to worry about actually progressing. Just use whatever reps/weights you had been using before.

Good luck!
